title: A Birthday Present for the Future: America's 250th Time Capsule!
summary: Imagine getting a birthday present that you can't open for 250 years! That's exactly what's happening for America's 250th birthday on July 4, 2026. Officials are burying a time capsule in Philadelphia, right near Independence Hall where the Declaration of Independence was signed. But this isn't just any box—it's a super-strong steel vault designed to survive floods, earthquakes, and centuries underground. Michael Berilla and his team at the National Institute of Standards and Technology built it. "Philadelphia would have to be six feet underwater for this time capsule to even possibly take on water," he said. That's like burying a treasure chest that can survive a flood taller than a person! So, what's inside? All 50 states, plus Washington, D.C., and U.S. territories, sent items to represent life in 2026. Utah went all out with 100 cards of famous people, 13 coins, documents, pins, and even two granite disks. Arkansas sent a real diamond! Maine added a bone from an endangered whale. Wisconsin contributed a feather from "Old Abe," a bald eagle that served with Union soldiers during the Civil War. California sent a computer chip and an AI-generated prediction of what the state might look like in 2276. The capsule will be buried under a special sculpture shaped like a segmented snake. It's inspired by Benjamin Franklin's famous 1754 "Join, or Die" cartoon, which showed that the colonies needed to unite. The National Park Service will pass down the location to future rangers so it can be found in 2276. When it's finally opened, the first thing people will see is a photo of the team and a letter that says: "Greetings from the living, breathing hearts and hands of 2026. We will have long since returned to dust, but our devotion, pride, and unwavering hope for what our world could become are alive right here inside this steel. We built this for you." So, what would you put in a time capsule for the future?
why_it_matters: This time capsule is like a message from our time to the future, showing that even though we'll be gone, our hopes and dreams will live on—just like how you might leave a note for your future self.

background_read: The Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776 at Independence Hall in Philadelphia, making the United States its own country.
Benjamin Franklin (one of America's founders and a clever inventor) drew the 'Join, or Die' snake cartoon in 1754.
The National Park Service cares for famous places like Independence Hall so they are protected for visitors.
Article_Structure: WHO: People from all 50 states, Washington D.C., and U.S. territories, along with the National Institute of Standards and Technology.
WHAT: A steel time capsule filled with cards, coins, a diamond, a whale bone, an eagle feather, a computer chip, and other items.
WHERE: Under a snake statue near Independence Hall in Philadelphia.
WHY: To mark the 250th anniversary of the United States and to let people in the year 2276 see what life was like in 2026.

perspectives.description: They believe time capsules are important because they freeze moments in time for future study.
States are excited to show off what makes them unique.
Some people think the capsule might never be found or that the items won't last 250 years.
